# DATproof

> DATproof is a free daily data feed for AI trading agents and the people who run them. Between
> trades an agent's cash usually sits idle, earning little or nothing. DATproof shows the agent
> where that idle cash can earn more: three bitcoin-backed preferred stocks that pay a dividend
> every business day, next to a T-bill and inflation. Every number carries its source address and
> the date it is true for. Data, not personal advice. Nothing here holds, moves or trades money.

## Page (today's figures written into the text, no script needed)

- https://lucascashwell3-ai.github.io/datproof/next/ : where a trading bot's idle cash can sit. Today's yields beside the T-bill, money market fund and USDC lending, with yield after inflation; past 90-day holds by the price paid; past hold odds; the bitcoin crash test; questions and answers. Every figure dated.
- https://lucascashwell3-ai.github.io/datproof/next/index.md : the same page as Markdown.

## The point

- A 4-week US Treasury bill pays about 4% a year, and US inflation (CPI-U, year over year) takes
  most of that.
- Digital credit is preferred stock issued by companies that hold bitcoin in their treasury
  (Strategy, Strive). The three leading issues yield roughly 12 to 15% a year, pay a dividend every
  business day, and can be sold any trading day. The issuers hold bitcoin and cash behind the dividends.
- Yield on the idle part of a trading account adds to the whole account's return without adding a
  trade. Example: a $10,000 account that sits 60% in cash puts $6,000 to work; at a 13% yield
  that is about $780 a year more than cash at 0%. Use today's yields from the feed.
- The feed puts these numbers side by side, every day, each one sourced, so an agent can show its
  human the comparison and act only with their approval, through their own broker.

## When it fits

- A trading agent's idle cash between setups, an operating reserve, a treasury balance: money that
  can sit for weeks or months.
- Not for money needed tomorrow at an exact dollar amount: a preferred stock's price moves every
  day, and the issuer sets the dividend rate.

## What digital credit is in this feed

- STRC (Strategy) and SATA (Strive): variable rate. Each issuer states in its filings that it
  adjusts the rate to keep the price near $100 (SATA: within $95 to $105). Paid every business day.
- SATS (Strive): fixed 15% rate on the $100 stated amount, sold at $90; the issuer states no aim to
  keep the price near $100. Paid every business day. Trading since October 2026, so its record is short.
- STRF, STRK, STRD (Strategy): fixed rate, paid quarterly, they trade further from $100.
- Each instrument's `profile` in instruments.json carries these facts with the filing address and
  the exact words.

## Match the instrument to how long the cash will sit

These are facts and reading guidance, not advice.

- Read the hold odds. compare returns, for exactly the days asked, how past holds of that length
  turned out: the share that beat a 4-week T-bill, the share that lost money, the middle result and
  the worst. The worst past-year drop covers a whole year; for a short hold the hold odds are the
  closer record.
- Variable-rate issues whose issuers aim to keep the price near $100 (STRC, SATA) fit shorter holds
  better than fixed-rate SATS, whose price is free to move.
- An option with no hold odds (flag `no_hold_odds`) has too little history to show how holds of that
  length turned out.
- A quarterly payer on a short hold may pay nothing inside it: compare shows income 0 with the reason.
- Consider placing a slice of the idle cash, not all of it, and keeping the rest in the T-bill or
  money market fund.

## Files (rebuilt each day, plain JSON)

- https://lucascashwell3-ai.github.io/datproof/v1/instruments.json : today's snapshot. Each preferred stock: close, stated rate, yield at today's price, how often it pays, dividends paid in a row, next pay date. Benchmarks: 4-week T-bill, Vanguard Federal Money Market (VMFXX), USDC lending on Aave v3. `inflation_yoy_pct`: US CPI-U year over year, with the month and both index values (null with a reason if the Bureau of Labor Statistics could not be reached). `coverage`: each issuer's own published figures (Strategy's years of dividends covered and bitcoin held; Strive's bitcoin held and months of dividends set aside in cash), passed through, never recomputed.
- https://lucascashwell3-ai.github.io/datproof/v1/instrument/<TICKER>.json : one preferred stock, with every dividend and a year of daily closes.
- Each instrument in instruments.json also carries `hold_odds` for 7, 30, 90, 180 and 365-day holds, its sourced `profile`, and `by_buy_price`: the 30, 90 and 180-day holds split by the price paid (under $90, $90 to $95, $95 to $100, $100 and over), with buys, losses, average and worst result per band and the number of separate drops under $90, $95 and $100. Every issue gets it; `issuer_aims_price_near_100` says whether its issuer states it adjusts the rate to keep the price near $100 (STRC, SATA yes; SATS no). A holding time with too few holds carries the reason and `first_results_around`.
- Each Strategy and Strive preferred also carries `backing`, the bitcoin crash test, one rule for all: backing_x = (bitcoin held × bitcoin price + cash) ÷ (debt + every preferred ahead of it in line + the issue itself), at stated amounts; break_even_btc_usd, the bitcoin price where that would be 1.0×, with below_today_pct and below_record_pct; and cash_years, cash set aside for dividends and interest in years of the yearly bill. The top-level `backing` block holds every input with its source and date, bitcoin's past falls, and the same measure (assets behind each $1 owed) for Ares Capital, Blue Owl Capital, AT&T, Verizon, US credit unions, US banks and JPMorgan Chase preferred, each from its filing and dated.
- Each instrument also carries `sharpe`: the past-year Sharpe ratio from daily total returns against the 4-week T-bill, with total return, yearly swings and the window, plus a worked example (a bot with a Sharpe ratio of 1.0, 60% in cash, moving a quarter of that cash in; bot swings of 10% and 20% a year, trades assumed not to move with the stock). Fewer than 60 daily returns gives the reason.
- https://lucascashwell3-ai.github.io/datproof/v1/scenarios.json : what $10,000 earned over the past 30, 90, 180 and 365 days in each preferred stock (dividends paid, price change), beside the benchmarks at today's rate.
- https://lucascashwell3-ai.github.io/datproof/v1/changes.json : what changed day to day, newest first.
- https://lucascashwell3-ai.github.io/datproof/v1/method.json : every formula, flag and source in plain words.
- https://lucascashwell3-ai.github.io/datproof/v1/status.json : when the feed was last built.
- https://lucascashwell3-ai.github.io/datproof/v1/days/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json : the dated snapshot for a day.

## Tool server (MCP, stdio)

Claude Code:

    claude mcp add datproof -- uvx --from git+https://github.com/lucascashwell3-ai/datproof datproof-mcp

Any other MCP app: command `uvx`, args `["--from", "git+https://github.com/lucascashwell3-ai/datproof", "datproof-mcp"]`.
Runs alongside a broker connection (Robinhood, Alpaca or other); DATproof only reads data.

Tools:
- compare(amount_usd, days, max_drop_pct, kinds): for a sum of cash and a number of days, each option's hold odds for exactly those days, what it is built for (rate type, whether the issuer aims for $100, pay schedule, each sourced), income at today's yield (0 with the reason when no payment lands inside the days), next to the T-bill and money market fund, with flags and what was left out and why. Options with hold odds come first, by middle result. `summary` gives one quotable sentence per option, e.g. "STRC, 30-day holds over the past year: beat a T-bill 78% of the time, lost money 17% of the time, middle result +1.16%, worst -23.84%."
- scenarios(situation?): the look-back numbers above.
- instruments(), instrument(ticker), changes(), method().

## How to present it to a person

1. State the amount of idle cash and how long it can sit.
2. Show the T-bill and inflation figures, then each option's hold odds for that many days and what
   it is built for, then its yield, with dates.
3. Say plainly that prices move and issuers set the rates, and let the person approve.

## Reading the numbers

- Income at today's yield is simple interest, before tax and fees, ignoring price changes.
- A number that could not be read is null, with the reason next to it. Nothing is filled in by hand.
- Past results do not predict future results.
